questions.q: In the following series of reactions identify the major products A and B respectively (bromobenzene -> SO3/H2SO4 -> A -> Br2/Fe -> B).
questions.explain: MARKS key: Br is o/p directing, so sulfonation goes para (A). Then Br2/Fe: the new Br goes ortho to Br and meta to SO3H - both directors agree - giving option B's product.

questions.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Nitration of benzene involves the following step (see image). Statement II: Use of Lewis base promotes the electrophilic substitution of benzene. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explain: MARKS key: The nitrating mixture protonates HNO3, which loses water to give NO2+. Lewis ACIDS (not bases) promote electrophile formation.

questions.q: Which of the following compound will most easily be attacked by an electrophile?
questions.explain: MARKS key: -OH donates by resonance and activates the ring most strongly; -CH3 is a weaker activator, Cl deactivates.

questions.q: Identify A and B in the following reaction sequence.
questions.explain: MARKS key: option A. Nitration fills the ring with NO2 groups, then NaOH replaces Br with OH and acid work-up gives picric acid.

questions.q: The arenium ion which is not involved in the bromination of aniline is:
questions.explain: MARKS key: NH2 is ortho/para-directing, so the meta-attack arenium ion is never formed.

questions.q: The correct order of reactivity in electrophilic substitution reaction of the following compounds is: A = benzene, B = toluene, C = chlorobenzene, D = nitrobenzene
questions.explain: MARKS key: Toluene is activated (hyperconjugation) above benzene; chlorobenzene is deactivated (-I), nitrobenzene strongly deactivated (-M).

questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of rate of aromatic electrophilic substitution reaction.
questions.explain: MARKS key: More electron density = faster EAS. (a) only +H of CH2, (b) -OH +R, (c) carbonyl pulls density away (slowest), (d) both -OH and -O- +R (fastest): c < a < b < d.

questions.q: Halogenation of which one of the following will yield m-substituted product with respect to methyl group as a major product?
questions.explain: MARKS key: OH directs better than CH3, so the electrophile goes ortho/para to OH - and the para-to-OH position is meta to CH3.

questions.q: Arrange the following in increasing order of reactivity towards nitration: A. p-xylene, B. bromobenzene, C. mesitylene, D. nitrobenzene, E. benzene
questions.explain: MARKS key: +M effect speeds up nitration, -M slows it: -NO2 strongly deactivates, -Br deactivates (but directs o/p), -CH3 activates. So nitrobenzene < bromobenzene < benzene < p-xylene < mesitylene = D < B < E < A < C.

questions.q: The intermediate X, in the following reaction (phenol + CHCl3/aq. NaOH, then NaOH, H+, giving salicylaldehyde) is:
questions.explain: MARKS key: In base phenol exists as phenoxide; the dichlorocarbene-derived intermediate carries ortho-CHCl2 on the phenoxide ring, which then hydrolyses to the aldehyde.

questions.q: The increasing order of the reactivity of the following compounds towards electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions is: I. chlorobenzene, II. toluene, III. acetophenone
questions.explain: MARKS key: Rate of E+ substitution rises with electron density: -COCH3 is strongly deactivating (III slowest), Cl deactivates (-I > +M), -CH3 activates (+H, +I). So III < I < II.

questions.q: In Friedel-Crafts alkylation of aniline, one gets:
options: alkylated product with ortho and para substitution
positively charged nitrogen at benzene ring
questions.explain: MARKS key: Aniline is basic and forms a salt with the Lewis-acid catalyst AlCl3; the N-positive complex deactivates the ring, so Friedel-Crafts alkylation does not occur.
